display.title: The Mysterious Mission
display.summary_short: The Baal Shem Tov takes his students to an empty field just to daven Mincha and say brachos, then reveals the story of the hidden Jew buried there.
display.summary_long: After the song "I Believe in Hashem", the storyteller describes the Baal Shem Tov's wondrous wagon, whose horses find their own way while the driver sleeps. One day it stops in an empty field. The Baal Shem Tov and his students daven Mincha, eat, say brachos, and pour a little mashkeh into the ground with a "L'chaim", then turn to go home. Seeing his students puzzled, the Baal Shem Tov tells the story behind the trip. A Torah scholar, Reb Yaakov, supported by his wife's store, is befriended by a scheming priest, who invites him to recover from an illness at his country home and bribes the cook to put non-kosher meat in his food. His spirit weakened, Reb Yaakov is drawn away from his people and marries the priest's daughter. Years later he finds his old watchman weeping: the man is a secret Jew, a Marrano, crying out on Yom Kippur. Reb Yaakov breaks down, flees to another land and does teshuvah; his wife, moved, later converts. The old watchman sets out on foot to do teshuvah too, but dies on the way, in that very field. The students' davening and brachos at his grave lift his neshamah to Gan Eden.
display.lesson: Kosher food guards a Jew's neshamah, and every Jew can return to Hashem. Davening and brachos said with care can help another neshamah.

advisories.note: A priest tricks a Torah scholar into eating non-kosher food and leaving his people; he later returns.
Marranos had to hide that they were Jews.
An old man dies on his journey to do teshuvah.
Angels debate whether a neshamah may enter Gan Eden.
A husband abandons his wife and lives among non-Jews.
